name: Kalyana Pasupatheeswarar Temple, Karur (Karuvur Anilai)
deity: Shiva as Pasupatheeswarar (Anilaiappar), with the goddess Alankaravalli (Soundaryanayaki)
period: A Paadal Petra Sthalam of Kongu Nadu on the Amaravathi, sung by Sambandar in the Tevaram (7th century)
summary: In the old city of Karur, where the divine cow Kamadhenu is said to have worshipped, Shiva is Pasupatheeswarar, Lord of the cow — the Karuvur Anilai sung by Sambandar and by the siddha Karuvurar.

sections.history: Karur, the Karuvur of Tamil literature, is one of the oldest cities of the Kongu country, set on the Amaravathi river, a tributary of the Kaveri. Its Shiva temple, called Anilai in the Tevaram, was sung by Sambandar and is one of the 276 Paadal Petra Sthalams and one of the seven of Kongu Nadu. Karur holds a large place in Shaiva memory: the Periya Puranam makes it the city of the Nayanar king Pugazh Chola and of Eripatha Nayanar, and it is the home of Karuvur Thevar, the siddha whose Thiruvisaippa hymns on this Lord stand in the ninth Tirumurai. Arunagirinathar later praised the temple in the Tiruppugazh.
sections.architecture: The temple stands in the heart of the town on Sannathi Street, a Dravidian complex with the sanctum of Pasupatheeswarar and a separate shrine for the goddess Alankaravalli. The lingam is held to lean slightly to one side, and on a few days each year, in the months of Masi and Panguni, the rays of the rising sun reach into the sanctum to touch it. Karuvurar, the siddha of Karur, is honoured within the temple, and its sacred waters are the Brahma theertham and the Amaravathi.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells that Kamadhenu, the wish-granting cow of the gods, came here and worshipped the Lord, bathing the lingam with her milk; so Shiva is called Pasupatheeswarar, Lord of the cow, and the shrine Anilai, the abode of the cow. Tradition adds that the Lord inclined to one side to listen to Karuvurar's songs. Karur is also where Eripatha Nayanar struck down the royal elephant that had scattered flowers gathered for Shiva — a story that ends in grace for both devotee and king.
sections.festivals: The days when sunlight falls on the lingam in Masi and Panguni draw devotees to the early-morning worship, when the first light enters the sanctum. Maha Shivaratri, Arudra Darshanam, the monthly Pradosham and the temple's annual festivals are kept as well; confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: Pasupatheeswarar is a town temple, busy with daily worship among Karur's streets and markets. Come early to stand before the leaning lingam, visit the goddess Alankaravalli, and pause to remember Karuvurar, whose songs are still sung here. If you can, time the visit for the sunlit mornings of Masi or Panguni.

visit.timings: Open daily in morning and evening sessions with a midday closure. Confirm current timings locally before visiting, especially for the sunlight days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left outside before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is not permitted inside the sanctum; in the outer corridors, ask the temple staff before taking pictures, especially of rituals.
visit.gettingThere: The temple is in central Karur, a short walk or auto ride from the bus stand. Karur Junction railway station is on the Tiruchirappalli–Erode line; Tiruchirappalli International Airport, about 80 km east, is the nearest airport.
